name: AWS Lambda
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in AWS Lambda as a competency should be able to architect, build, and operate large-scale event-driven serverless systems where Lambda is the core compute layer. They can reason precisely about the Lambda execution model at depth — cold/warm start lifecycle, SnapStart, provisioned vs reserved vs unreserved concurrency, burst limits and account-level throttling, execution-environment reuse, and ephemeral storage — and use that model to tune latency, throughput, and cost under production load. They design robust event-driven architectures across API Gateway, ALB, S3, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis, SQS/SNS, EventBridge, and Step Functions, choosing correct invocation semantics (sync/async/poll-based), and engineer for at-least-once delivery: idempotency keys and dedupe stores, partial-batch failure reporting (ReportBatchItemFailures), event source mapping tuning (batch size, window, parallelization factor, bisect-on-error), DLQs and redrive policies, destinations, and poison-pill isolation. They implement advanced handler patterns — connection reuse, init-phase optimization, structured logging with correlation IDs, embedded metrics (EMF), distributed tracing (X-Ray/OpenTelemetry), graceful timeout budgeting, and safe retries with backoff and jitter — and can debug complex production failures from logs, traces, and metrics alone. They design secure multi-account/multi-env deployments: least-privilege execution roles, resource-based policies, VPC-attached functions with ENI/scaling implications, RDS Proxy, KMS encryption, and secrets rotation. They package and ship functions with layers, containers-as-images, and IaC (Terraform, SAM, CDK), run blue/green and canary releases with versions, aliases, and CodeDeploy, wire CI/CD with automated tests (unit, integration against emulators such as LocalStack, and contract tests), and enforce operational governance: concurrency quotas, cost monitoring, alarming, runbooks, and incident response. They know Lambda's hard limits and failure modes cold, can articulate when Lambda is the wrong tool, and can lead migration and refactoring of existing systems onto (or off of) serverless compute.
long_scope: Exhaustive competency scope for AWS Lambda at ADVANCED proficiency (6-10 years). Sections: 1) Execution Model Internals & Concurrency — cold/warm lifecycle, SnapStart, provisioned/reserved concurrency, burst and account throttling, environment reuse. 2) Event-Driven Architecture & Invocation Semantics — sync/async/poll-based sources, event source mapping tuning, EventBridge/Step Functions orchestration, fan-out patterns. 3) Reliability Engineering — idempotency, dedupe stores, ReportBatchItemFailures, DLQ/redrive design, destinations, poison-pill isolation, retry/backoff strategy. 4) Advanced Handler & Runtime Patterns — init-phase optimization, connection reuse, timeout budgeting, structured logging, EMF metrics, X-Ray/OpenTelemetry tracing. 5) Security & Networking at Scale — least-privilege execution roles, resource policies, multi-account patterns, VPC/ENI implications, RDS Proxy, KMS, secrets rotation. 6) Packaging, Deployment & IaC — layers, container images, Terraform/SAM/CDK, versions/aliases, blue-green and canary via CodeDeploy, CI/CD integration. 7) Testing & Local Emulation — unit/integration/contract testing, LocalStack-based end-to-end validation, chaos and failure injection. 8) Performance & Cost Optimization — memory/CPU tuning, concurrency tuning, batch sizing, cost modelling, when-not-Lambda decisions. 9) Production Operations & Governance — quotas, alarms, runbooks, incident response, migration leadership, documentation and standards.
